facts.statement: Tikisuchus was the first rauisuchid fossil discovered in Asia, found in the Late Triassic Tiki Formation of central India.
facts.quote: It is known from the Late Triassic Tiki Formation in the Shahdol District of central India and was the first rauisuchid to have been found in Asia.

facts.statement: The type species Tikisuchus romeri was named to honor the American paleontologist Alfred Romer.
facts.quote: The type species is T. romeri, named in honor of American paleontologist Alfred Romer.

facts.statement: Only one specimen, ISI R 305, is known, containing the skull and some postcranial bones of a young individual.
facts.quote: Tikisuchus is known only from one specimen, called ISI R 305, which consists of the skull and some postcranial elements of a young individual.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus possessed a skull that was exceptionally large compared to other rauisuchids.
facts.quote: Compared to other rausuchids, the skull of Tikisuchus was very large.

facts.statement: The skull length of Tikisuchus was approximately 40% of the length of the presacral vertebral column.
facts.quote: The skull's length is around 40% of the length of the presacral area between the head and the sacrum.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus had large, recurved, and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth are large, recurved and serrated.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus had two rows of osteoderms, or bony scutes, running along its back.
facts.quote: Like other rauisuchids, it has rows of osteoderms, or bony scutes, along its back. There are two rows of osteoderms.

facts.statement: The rectangular osteoderms of Tikisuchus articulated tightly with adjacent ones in an imbricate pattern.
facts.quote: Each osteoderm is rectangular in shape and imbricates, or articulates tightly, with the ones around it.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: The horizon from which remains have been found is Carnian in age.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tikisuchus was a large terrestrial predator that likely shared its habitat with theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Both Tikisuchus and the theropods were large terrestrial predators, and, having been found at the same locality, likely came in close contact with one another.

facts.statement: Potential prey for Tikisuchus included rhynchosaurs, trilophosaurs, dicynodonts, and aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Possible prey would have included rhynchosaurs, trilophosaurs, dicynodonts, and aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Recent studies debate the cause of rauisuchid decline, suggesting dinosaurs only became dominant after the Triassic-Jurassic extinction removed competing large archosaurs.
facts.quote: However, more recent studies suggest that dinosaurs gained dominance only after the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event in a case of opportunism with no other large archosaurs such as rauisuchids to compete with.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus is classified as an extinct genus of rauisuchid archosauromorph.
facts.quote: Tikisuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchid archosauromorph.

facts.statement: Tikisuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
